request.description:
## Request body parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| name | string | Specify the name of your keyring. | Azure keyring |
| description | string | (Optional) Specify the description for your keyring. | Keyring for Azure connectors |
| keyring_type | string | Specify the value for your keyring type. See Fetch all keyrings for the list of valid values. | azure_key_vault |
| value.connector_type | string | Specify the connector for which you want to create a keyring. Each credential vault supports a certain set of connectors. | microsoft_azure_sql_database_onprem |
| value.vault_instance | string | Specify the name of your credential vault instance. | Azure key vault instance |
| value.aws_secret_name | string | Specify the name of the secret stored in AWS Secrets Manager. Applicable only when keyring_type is aws_secret_manager. | prod/db/connector-creds |
| value.credentials_auth_key.auth_type | string | Specify the authentication type(s) for your connector. See the keyring metadata API for the valid values for your connector. | Service Principal |
| value.credentials_key_name.user | string | Example field name for a username and password-based credential vault. Check the keyring metadata API for the actual field names your keyring type expects. | john.doe |
| value.credentials_key_name.password | string | Example field name for a username and password-based credential vault. Check the keyring metadata API for the actual field names your keyring type expects. | P@ssw0rd!123 |

Note: value.credentials_key_name is shown here with one example field pair (user/password), for a username and password-based credential vault. Other credential vaults and connectors expect different field names entirely, such as token, secret, aws_access_key, or aws_secret_key. Always check the keyring metadata API for the exact fields your selected keyring type expects before sending this request.
